systems.name: Product catalog
systems.role: lists what is sold and the technical data needed to switch it on
cannot_observe: which version of an offer applied to an order: the catalog holds validity dates only

systems.name: Order manager
systems.role: receives the order and splits it into service orders
cannot_observe: when each state change happened: a row holds the current state and its creation time

systems.name: Process orchestrator
systems.role: runs the tasks in order and hands some to people

systems.name: Activation system
systems.role: switches the service on in the network; can fail and retry

terms.name: Manual handling of the failed activations
Daily follow-up while the order waits

scenario.fix: retry a failed activation automatically within 24 h
scenario.mechanism: a retry clears the failures whose error code the config classes as transient; failures with a code it does not classify are assumed to stay

findings.recommendation: Retry a failed activation automatically, or raise it to a queue a person owns, within the retry window.

findings.title: Missing catalog attribute forces a manual task
findings.plain_summary: The product's technical spec lacks a value the activation system needs, so a person fills it in by hand on every order.

terms.name: Manual check that the missing attribute makes necessary

scenario.fix: add the missing attribute to the spec of the offer version
scenario.mechanism: the manual task exists only because the attribute is missing, so every order that ran it is assumed not to need it

findings.recommendation: Add the missing attribute to the spec of the offer version, so the activation system gets it without a manual step. The hours are freeable capacity, not savings.

terms.name: Manual handling of the stuck orders
Daily follow-up while the order is stuck

scenario.fix: give every watched timer a compensation task or a queue a person owns
scenario.mechanism: an expired timer then leads somewhere at once, so no order is assumed to stay stuck past the threshold

findings.recommendation: Give every timer an exit: a compensation task or a queue a person owns, so an expired timer never leaves an order waiting.

findings.title: Duplicate service order
findings.plain_summary: A second service order exists for the same order line. When activation failed, a retry created a new order instead of reusing the first.

findings.recommendation: Make the retry reuse the existing service order, and confirm in billing the orders whose duplicate reached activation.
